verification_report.summary: All 17 supplied items were checked sequentially, including the curvewise definition, the small deductions in each proof, and the hypotheses of the external results. No critical error or proof gap was found. The rig-smooth curve envelope satisfies harmonic comparison; regularization on the interior and the cited boundary-extension property cover all points. Perfected scalar extension, reduction, and bijective normalization give the required homeomorphisms, after which finite-surjective and scalar descent apply. The obstacle corollaries correctly handle local upper bounds and the empty family. These uses match [Gubler–Rabinoff](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.13548v2). The affine proof correctly constructs the shrinking analytic tube, establishes its finite Gauss boundary, and applies harmonic pullback and the affinoid maximum principle. Its projection is quasi-smooth and boundaryless on the chosen open neighborhood, so [Ducros, Corollary 6.2.5](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~antoine.ducros/Families-Berko.pdf) provides the openness needed to bound the ambient regularization. The three topological regularization lemmas are valid, including the compact-fiber maximum and the case of value minus infinity. Scalar projections meet the closedness and compactness hypotheses; Banach-spectrum compactness is also stated in [Berkovich’s notes, Fact 1.2.6](https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~vova/Trieste_2009.pdf). The canonical section uses exactly the multiplicative tensor norm and continuity supplied by [Poineau, Definition 3.2, Corollaries 3.7 and 3.14, and Remark 3.13](https://poineau.users.lmno.cnrs.fr/Textes/Angie.pdf). The retraction identities, fiberwise-constancy equivalences, ordered defect splitting, and local-failure inclusion then follow as written. Sheafiness supplies the final curve witness. The nonopenness example matches [Poineau–Turchetti](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.09043), where the preprint labels I.5.2 and I.5.4 correspond to the cited published labels 5.6.2 and 5.6.4. The proof correctly limits its affine conclusion to ground-field curvewise psh unless scalar compatibility is assumed; it does not infer psh preservation by the continuous retraction.
